title: Console UX: represent overload events + load shedding in dashboards and customer analytics
creator: Henry Cho
description:
Context
We are rolling out layered overload protection (admission control + circuit breakers + runtime shed points). During overload we will intentionally return 429/503 with Redwood-specific overload error codes and Retry-After instead of ambiguous 5xx/timeouts.

This ticket defines how overload events and overload-protected errors show up in the Redwood Console (dashboards + customer-visible analytics) so customers can:
1) Understand what happened (they were shed vs we were broken)
2) Take action (retry/backoff, reduce concurrency, switch models/regions if configured)
3) Correlate impact (by route/model/region) without creating confusion that "Redwood was down".

Goals
- Make overload behavior legible in the Console without requiring customers to read incident threads.
- Clearly distinguish:
  - Overload-protected responses (intentional shedding / temporary unavailability)
  - Internal failures (unexpected 5xx)
  - Customer-side throttling (quota/rate-limit)
- Provide drill-down into: model, region, endpoint/route, tier (Hosted vs Dedicated where relevant), streaming vs non-streaming.
- Align with SLO accounting changes ("overload-protected" errors may be tracked separately from internal errors).

Non-goals
- Designing a full incident/status system in Console (Status Page remains source of truth for outages).
- Creating bespoke per-customer overload dashboards beyond the standard panels (support via filters).

Primary user stories
- As a customer engineer, I see a spike in 503s and want to know if it’s due to overload shedding and what to do next.
- As a platform engineer, I want to correlate latency degradation with shedding activation (did we stabilize p99 by shedding?).
- As a customer success/support engineer, I need a canonical screenshotable view to explain an event to a customer.

Proposed UX (draft)
A) Request Analytics: error breakdown enhancements
- Add a first-class grouping: "Response outcome" with three top-level buckets:
  1) Success
  2) Overload-protected (intentional)
  3) Failed (internal)
  4) Customer-throttled (quota/rate limit) (if already present, just ensure it’s visually distinct)
- For "Overload-protected", show sub-breakdown by Redwood overload error code (from ADR-0147), e.g.:
  - OVERLOAD_EDGE_ADMISSION
  - OVERLOAD_ROUTING_BREAKER_OPEN
  - OVERLOAD_RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL
  - OVERLOAD_RUNTIME_MEMORY_PRESSURE
(Exact naming to match ENG-4823 / shared schema.)
- On hover/tooltips: include plain-language description + suggested customer action + whether Retry-After is expected.

B) Time series annotations for "overload active"
- When shed rate crosses a threshold (definition owned by SRE/Obs), show a shaded band or event markers on latency/error charts:
  - Label: "Overload protection active"
  - Click opens side panel with summary (start/end time, peak shed rate, top impacted models/routes/regions)
- Copy guidance: Avoid language like "outage" unless status-page incident exists.

C) New panel: "Overload protection" overview widget (console dashboard)
- Small summary card on the Hosted API dashboard (and possibly per-model dashboard):
  - Current state: Normal / Elevated shedding / Active shedding
  - Last 24h: total shed requests (%), top reason, top model/region
  - Link: "View details" -> drill-down page
- If a customer has Dedicated + Hosted, keep the widget scoped to the environment they’re viewing; don’t imply Dedicated pools are affected unless they are.

D) Drill-down page: "Overload events"
- Table of recent overload windows (auto-detected) with columns:
  - Time window
  - Environment (Hosted / Dedicated)
  - Region
  - Primary driver (top overload reason code)
  - Impact summary (peak shed %, peak p99)
  - Top endpoints/models
- Clicking a row opens a detail view:
  - "What happened" summary
  - Charts: shed rate, breaker transitions (if customer-visible), p95/p99 latency, error mix
  - "What you can do" box:
    - Recommended retry strategy (exponential backoff + jitter)
    - Respect Retry-After
    - Reduce concurrency / cap max in-flight
    - If configured: enable fallback region/model; otherwise link to docs

E) Streaming-specific behavior
- If streaming disconnects are surfaced as errors, they must be classified correctly:
  - If disconnect occurs due to shedding: show as "Overload-protected" with a distinct reason (if available)
  - Otherwise: treat as "Failed" and recommend contacting support if persistent
- Avoid double-counting: a single request should not appear as both a disconnect error and an overload-protected response.

F) Billing/usage wording (coordination)
- Add a tooltip/help link near Overload-protected counts: "Overload-protected responses are not successful completions; refer to billing docs for whether tokens are billed." (Exact statement to be confirmed with Product/Finance; do not invent policy in UI.)

Information architecture + visual language
- Use neutral, action-oriented labeling:
  - Preferred: "Overload-protected" / "Load shedding"
  - Avoid: "failover" unless we actually served a fallback successfully
  - Avoid: "incident" unless explicitly tied to a status page incident ID
- Color guidance:
  - Success: existing
  - Overload-protected: warning/amber (distinct from red)
  - Failed/internal: red
  - Customer-throttled: purple/gray (whatever current rate-limit color is)

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Do we expose breaker states (open/half-open/closed) directly to customers, or keep it aggregated as "overload protection active"?
   - Current leaning (PM/SRE): do not expose raw breaker state; expose aggregated shedding + reason codes to reduce confusion.
2) Event detection threshold: what constitutes an "overload window" for the table?
   - Proposal: shed_rate > X% for Y minutes, with hysteresis, aligned to alerting windows (ENG-4830).
3) Dedicated alignment: do we show overload events for Dedicated in the same UI?
   - Proposal: yes, but clearly labeled and scoped; Dedicated customers expect predictable behavior; avoid implying cross-tenant impact.
4) Retry guidance copy: should we show customer guidance inline vs link to docs only?
   - Proposal: short inline guidance + link to canonical docs.

Acceptance criteria
- Figma draft(s) for:
  - Updated error breakdown component (incl. overload-protected bucket + reason-code breakdown)
  - Overload annotations on time series
  - Overload overview widget
  - Overload events table + detail panel
- Copy deck (strings) reviewed by PM (Henry Cho) and SRE (Rafael Mendes) for correctness.
- Handoff notes specify required data fields (reason code, Retry-After presence, region/model/route labels) and any constraints on cardinality.

References
- PRD: PRD Hosted Overload Protection Customer Experience (Confluence)
- ADR-0147: Overload error taxonomy and HTTP mapping
- Dashboard spec: Overload protection dashboards (Confluence)
- Dependencies: ENG-4830 (dashboards), ENG-4823 (error payload), ENG-4829 (metrics/traces)
comments: 2025-12-10 — Henry Cho (Product): Creating as a follow-up to PM-911. We need a customer-facing view that makes 429/503 during shedding "understandable" and clearly not an outage. Please prioritize avoiding confusing language (customers are currently filing tickets when they see 503s even if system is healthy but saturated).

2025-12-16 — Nora Ahmed (Design): Drafted initial IA: keep this under Analytics > Requests, with an Overload tab + event table. Question for SRE/Obs: do we have a consistent definition of an "overload window" we can show as an event? Otherwise this becomes a raw chart with no summary.

2025-12-18 — Sergio Costa (Observability): We can compute windows off shed_rate + breaker_open signals. Need to keep labels bounded; route/model/region ok, but avoid customer_id labels in any shared charts. For customer-facing, should be filtered to their tenant anyway.

2025-12-20 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): +1 to not exposing raw breaker state as a customer-first object. We should instead surface reason codes + Retry-After guidance. Breaker state is too easy to misinterpret (half-open etc.) and risks support noise.

2026-01-03 — Allison Grant (Observability): Please ensure any UI that breaks down by reason code uses the same canonical enum names as the API error schema (ENG-4823). Also note: some shed points won’t always have Retry-After; UI should not promise it’s present on every response.

2026-01-08 — Nora Ahmed (Design): Updated draft: "Overload-protected" is amber, distinct from internal failure red. Added tooltips with guidance and link to docs. Pending: Dedicated alignment decision (ENG-4837) and final copy approval.

2026-01-12 — Henry Cho (Product): Reviewed draft; looks good. Two tweaks: (1) Make sure we explicitly separate quota/rate-limit from overload shedding (customers conflate these). (2) Avoid any copy that implies refunds/billing policy; link out instead.
